% RETURN, REBASED · EOD 2026-11-13
DEFENSIVES LEADCyclicals -6.4% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

Defensives are winning and the market is paying up for safety, a rotation you should respect rather than fade. Health care leads with XLV up 8.56% in a month and 21.44% year to date, while staples add 7.31% and real estate 6.94%. Utilities gain 5.56%. On the other side, tech is the wreck: XLK is down 10.58%, communication services down 1.92%, and energy down 3.95%. The top of the board is where cash flows are predictable, and the bottom is where the growth story lives.

The theme data confirms a violent unwinding of the speculative edge. Semis shed 16.2% in a month and AI infra 16.0%, software 13.1%, cyber 12.7%, quantum 12.4%, uranium 12.1%. Those same baskets carry fat year-to-date gains of 42.4%, 59.7%, 65.2% and 8.3%, so this is profit-taking in the crowded winners, not a verdict on their businesses. Mag 7 is down 5.9% and bank stocks only up 5.2%, which says the selling is concentrated in long-duration growth. GLP-1 is the exception at 13.2% in a month, a narrow defensive-growth pocket inside health care.

The stretched ratios show the defensive bid is extreme and the cyclical trade is washed out. XLV/SPY sits at a z-score of 2.51, in the top 99% of its yearly range (z-score measures how many standard deviations a ratio is from its average). XLI/XLP is at -2.44, in the bottom 1%, and BKLN/HYG is at 2.4, the very top of its range, a sign you are being paid to sit in safer credit. The move into safety is crowded. When health care outruns the broad market by this much, the easy money has been made in defensives and the next leg likely belongs to the beaten-down cyclicals.

Defensive leadership is extreme, and the cyclical-versus-defensive ratios are pinned at historic lows, setting up a snap-back risk.

BULL

The risk-on read is that cyclicals are washed out and cheap: XLI/XLP at the 1% mark of its range and XME/XLB at 1% are the kind of extremes that precede a rotation back into industrials and materials. Banks up 5.2% and financials up 7.63% show the credit machine is still running.

BEAR

The defensive read is that the market is fleeing the growth complex for a reason: XLV at 8.56% and XLP at 7.31% in a month with semis down 16.2% is a de-risking, and BKLN/HYG at the 100th place in its range says investors want safety in credit, not yield.

TELL

Watch XLI/XLP off the 1% mark and XLV/SPY off the 99% mark; a break back toward the middle resolves the rotation into cyclicals, a fresh low in XLI/XLP confirms the defensive flight.

⚠ Sector performance shows defensives leading hard: XLV **+8.56%**, XLP **+7.31%**, XLRE **+6.94%** in a month. vs The pro-cyclical ratios XLI/XLP and XME/XLB sit at the **1%** mark of their yearly range.: Defensive leadership and cyclical ratios at historic lows are the same signal from two angles, so they agree; trust the defensive read until XLI/XLP lifts off the **1%** floor.
⚠ The defensive bid is broad, with health care, staples and real estate all up more than **6.9%** in a month. vs Gold versus the dollar (GLD/UUP) is at a z-score of **-1.77** and the bottom of its range, so the classic haven is not confirming the flight to safety.: A safety rotation without a gold bid is a dollar-driven de-risking rather than a fear trade; trust the sector performance and treat gold's weakness as a dollar story, which caps how far the defensive rotation runs.

The confirmed trend is the defensive and quality bid, and the mean-reversion candidates are the cyclical and commodity ratios at the floor. XLV/SPY at 2.51 z and top 99% of range is stretched but backed by real leadership (+8.56% month for XLV), so treat it as trend, not a fade.

BKLN/HYG at 2.4 (top of range) and SHY/TLT at 1.79 (top 94%) confirm investors are hiding in short-dated safety. The genuine reversion candidates are in the bottom: GDXJ/GDX at -3.3 z in the bottom of its range, XLI/XLP at -2.44 (bottom 1%), XME/XLB at -2.46 (bottom 1%), and IWF/IWD at -2.25 (bottom 2%).

Those are the ratios a sharp desk watches for a snap-back: small-cap gold miners versus large, industrials versus staples, metals versus materials. The one to distrust is GLD/UUP at -1.77 in the bottom of its range, which says gold is weak against the dollar even as the defensive trade runs.

That inconsistency is the crack.
